column1: # Upstream refusals that decide a cell's outcome before its wire rows are
# read. scripts/wire_watch/refusal.py loads this table; the first row, in
# table order, that matches any of a cell's upstream error rows wins, so a
# more specific row must come before a more general one.
# Columns (tab-separated, header row below this comment block):
#   egress    bedrock -- the cell's lane is a Bedrock lane (listed in
#             models.tsv: Invoke, Converse and the Mantle vocabularies);
#             other -- any other lane
#   status    the upstream HTTP status the error row carries, or * for any
#   match     -              the status alone decides
#             key-expired    the cell's short-term Bedrock key had passed
#                            the expiry encoded in it when the cell ended,
#                            so whatever the upstream answered, the key
#                            is why
#             phrase:<text>  the error excerpt contains <text> verbatim
#   outcome   NOT_RUN or FAILED
#   reason    the outcome's reason token
#   source    where the status or the phrase is documented or recorded. A
#             bedrock row cites a docs.aws.amazon.com page, or a recorded
#             bedrock_*.json fixture for a phrase row
# A Bedrock 403 reaches the evidence as routectl's own action-only string
# ("bedrock access denied[: missing IAM action ...]", built in
# crates/routectl-providers/src/aws_error.rs), never as the AWS body, so the
# 403 rows key on the status alone. A Bedrock 400 ValidationException
# carries its exception name in a response header the excerpt never holds,
# so the model-access 400 row keys on the recorded message instead of the
# exception name; any other 400 is a wire result, not a refusal.
egress
bedrock
bedrock
bedrock
bedrock
bedrock
